course_name_original: Sistemas fluidomecánicos y materiales avanzados para el transporte
course_name_en: Fluid-mechanical systems and advanced materials for transport
prerequisites: To enroll in this course, it is necessary to have passed or be enrolled in all subjects from years prior to the year in which this course is located.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and competencies in the field of industrial engineering in the Mechanics specialty.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Knowledge and abilities for the application of materials engineering.
Autonomous learning and work.
Teamwork.
Knowledge of complex flows and their application in the design and operation of vehicles for land, sea, and air transport.
Ability for the design of the different fluid installations of the main components of vehicles for land, sea, and air transport.
Ability for the design of the different fluid installations of the transport industry and related industries.
Knows the basic requirements of the transport industry and related industries for an adequate selection of materials.
Knows the evolution of the different types of materials used in the main components of vehicles for land, sea, and air transport and the processes for their possible shaping.
Knows the different types of materials.
Selects the most suitable materials for different applications within the transport industry and related industries.
Knows the new materials used in this industry.
Understands the specifications for material purchasing.
Effectively identifies the causes of in-service failure derived from the material used.
Analyzes and proposes operational solutions to problems in the field of materials engineering.
Drafts texts with the appropriate structure for communication objectives. Presents the text to an audience with appropriate strategies and means.
Demonstrates communication and teamwork skills.
Identifies own information needs and uses available means, spaces, and services to design and execute searches appropriate to the thematic area.
Completes assigned tasks based on basic guidelines given by the professor, deciding the duration of parts, including personal contributions, and expanding information sources.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I: FLUIDMECHANICAL SYSTEMS FOR TRANSPORT
1. EXTERNAL FLOWS. FORCES ON BODIES IN A FLUID. DRAG. LIFT.
2. COMPRESSIBLE FLOWS. OPERATION OF CONVERGENT AND DIVERGENT NOZZLES. FLOW IN DUCTS WITHOUT FRICTION AND WITH HEAT ADDITION.
BLOCK II: ADVANCED MATERIALS IN THE TRANSPORT INDUSTRY
1. REQUIREMENTS IN THE TRANSPORT INDUSTRY: Regulations. Vehicle weight reduction.
2. EVOLUTION OF MATERIALS AND THEIR TECHNOLOGIES. - Mechanisms for increasing resistance. Encasing. Material selection criteria: Corrosion and corrosion protection.

3. ADVANCED MATERIALS IN THE AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY. Materials for bodywork (Advanced steels, light alloys, composite materials). Materials for mechanical systems. Materials for interior lining. Recycling.
4. MATERIALS IN OTHER TRANSPORT INDUSTRIES. Railway. Naval construction. Aeronautical industry.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practicals (Block II) reports and participation
Problem solving and/or exercises (Block I) partial tests
Objective questions exam (Block II, final test)

assessment_rules: To pass, a total grade above 50% is required, as a weighted average of both blocks; if minimums for any part are not met, the maximum final grade will be 4.9. Block I continuous assessment uses grades P1, P2, P3 (30% each) and BP (10%), all requiring a minimum of 4.0/10, with 80% practical test completion, for an overall 5.0/10 to pass. Block II continuous assessment requires a minimum of 40% in each test and an overall average above 50%. In extraordinary calls, Block I allows repeating failed tests while Block II retains practical grades and requires a final test; unethical behavior results in a 0.0 for the course.
